exposure: pregnancy-associated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
outcome: pregnancy-associated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
intensive care unit admission during the perinatal period
cohort: The study included 34,392 women with pregnancy-related hospitalizations from 2009 to 2020 from the perinatal database of seven multicenters.
finding: Pregnancy-associated HFpEF is significantly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes such as intensive care unit admission and postpartum hemorrhage, and risk factors for HFpEF include old maternal age, multiple pregnancy, rheumatic disease, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
